decision_reason: This is Development Gateway's public Aid Management Platform source, whose official product history says it was conceived and created in collaboration with the Governments of Ethiopia and India and public/international institutions including the World Bank, UNDP, and OECD. The exact repository is publicly available under GPL-3.0, and its first root license was added to the existing source tree in 2018. Development Gateway documents current AMP support and 25+ country implementations; a government-hosted Malawi deployment identifies the live DCIMS system as Development Gateway-built and updated monthly. No catalog entry was added.

government_provenance.note: Development Gateway's first-party AMP history says the platform was conceived and created in collaboration with the Governments of Ethiopia and India, OECD, World Bank, and UNDP. It is a product-specific public-sector co-development relationship, not an inference from DPG registry metadata.

public_source.note: The exact public repository exposes the Aid Management Platform Java application, installation/architecture documentation, and development source without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The repository root LICENSE contains the complete GNU GPL version 3 grant (GPL-3.0, without an added later-version clause) for first-party AMP source in this repository. The first root license-file commit is dated 2018-09-05; dependencies and external country data/configurations retain their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: The Government of Malawi's live Development Cooperation Information Management System page identifies the service as developed by Development Gateway, says government and donor users use it for daily project management, and states data are updated monthly. Development Gateway's current AMP page documents country implementations, ongoing support, and training; the repository links an installation guide.

product_identity: Aid Management Platform (AMP), Development Gateway's Java-based aid information management system and software component of its broader Aid Management Program
agency: Government of Ethiopia (Ministry of Finance and Economic Development) and Government of India as co-development partners, with OECD, World Bank, and UNDP; product steward Development Gateway
geography: Global country deployments; product originated through work with Ethiopia and India
license: GPL-3.0 for first-party AMP source in this repository; dependencies, country configurations/data, and separately deployed services retain their own terms
family_note: This repository is the AMP software component, not every implementation or country configuration in Development Gateway's Aid Management Program. Country-specific data, integrations, and external dependencies are not assumed to be covered by the root grant.
status_note: The public source history includes code before the root LICENSE was added. The 2018-09-05 commit linked above adds the complete GPL-3.0 LICENSE and documentation to that existing code, so source creation date is not substituted for the first public licensed-source year. No catalog entry was added.

decision_reason: Development Gateway's first-party technical account documents a specific Open Contracting Portal co-developed with the Government of Makueni County, and the repository has public source and an MIT grant. However, the repository does not expose GitHub releases, its root license history begins with a 2015 commit that contains only the license and a short README (not the application source), and current government deployment/support of the exact code could not be verified. Hold pending a defensible first public licensed-source year and current product-specific support/deployment evidence.

government_provenance.note: Development Gateway says it developed the Government of Makueni County Open Contracting Portal in partnership with the county, and describes the specific analytics, procurement-data and OCDS functions reflected by this product. The county's official page confirms the portal launch. The DPG record links this exact repository as the submitted product source; no government funding claim is inferred from Hivos/Hewlett support.

public_source.note: The exact public repository exposes the Open Contracting Portal application source and documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The repository root LICENSE is a full MIT grant for the first-party portal source in this repository, consistent with the README. The grant does not cover external libraries, the underlying Open Contracting Data Standard, or separately deployed data/configuration.

primary_evidence.note: Official Development Gateway and Makueni sources establish a production launch in 2019, and the official OC Portal site still serves installation/user documentation. The repository has no GitHub releases and no current use, support, or deployment signal for this exact code was verified; the Makueni instance could not be checked during this review, so current status remains unresolved rather than presumed absent.

product_identity: Open Contracting Portal (OC Portal), a procurement-document and data-entry/analytics portal that publishes structured data using OCDS; the Makueni deployment was built with the county using Development Gateway's OCE/DG Toolkit components
agency: Government of Makueni County, Kenya, in product development partnership with Development Gateway; Hivos supported the implementation (not a government agency)
geography: Makueni County, Kenya; current reuse in other jurisdictions is not established for this exact code
license: MIT for first-party source in this repository; third-party libraries, OCE/DG Toolkit components outside this repository, and instance data/configuration retain their own terms
family_note: The Makueni technical account describes the deployment as using the Open Contracting Explorer framework and DG Toolkit modules. This review is limited to the assigned ocportal repository; linked frameworks and other county-specific deployments are not presumed to share its license or current status.
status_note: The 2015-07-22 initial repository commit https://github.com/devgateway/ocportal/commit/2ee36c48b792df9994980c16da8ceba199ae3ad2 adds only LICENSE and a short README, not application source, so that date does not establish the first public licensed-code year. Official sources document the Makueni launch in 2019 and historical user-facing functionality; the repository has no GitHub Releases and current deployment/support was not verified. Hold; no catalog entry was added.

decision_reason: The assigned repository is the public SistemaUnicoSCU codebase from Italy's Department for Youth Policies and Universal Civil Service (PCM-DGSCU), including the Helios/Futuro workflows and the DOL online application. The official Developers Italia record names the department as publisher and manager and links this exact repository as source; the live official DOL service is taking applications under a current 2026 call and provides applicant instructions. The first public source code appeared in 2022 under GPL-3.0; the repository's current first-party grant is AGPL-3.0-only. The repository metadata lists mandatory third-party dependencies, including proprietary products, which are not covered by the repository grant. No catalog entry was added.

government_provenance.note: The official DTD/AgID Developers Italia record identifies the Dipartimento per le politiche giovanili e il Servizio civile universale (PCM) as publisher and PCM-DGSCU as manager, links this exact repository as source, and describes the application as prepared by the department with the Servizio civile system. The repository README identifies itself as DGSCU's Sistema Unico SCU.

public_source.note: The assigned repository is public and contains application code, database scripts, web services, the DOL application, and user manuals without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The current root LICENSE contains the full GNU Affero GPL version 3 grant (AGPL-3.0-only) for first-party repository code. The root license began as GPL-3.0 in 2022 and was changed to AGPL-3.0 in 2024. The repository's publiccode.yml separately lists mandatory third-party dependencies including Aspose.PDF, Aspose.Words, Microsoft SQL Server, CrystalReports, and Ionic.Zip; those components are not covered by this source grant.

primary_evidence.note: The official citizen-facing service is live and currently advertises a 2026 call for 3,767 volunteer positions, with SPID/CIE access instructions. The official software record marks SistemaUnicoSCU stable and used by the department, and the exact repository contains versioned user manuals and technical documentation.

product_identity: SistemaUnicoSCU, the department's web application suite for the Italian Universal Civil Service, comprising Helios/Futuro workflows and the Domanda On Line (DOL) applicant service
agency: Dipartimento per le politiche giovanili e il Servizio civile universale (PCM-DGSCU), Presidency of the Council of Ministers, Italy
license: AGPL-3.0-only for current first-party source in the repository; the initial 2022 code commit followed a root GPL-3.0 grant. Required third-party proprietary dependencies listed in publiccode.yml are outside this grant and may impose separate deployment terms.
family_note: The repository is one suite containing SistemaUnicoSCU workflows and DOL, not a standalone authentication library. Manuals are under Manuali Utente. The root AGPL grant is scoped to repository first-party source, not dependencies named in publiccode.yml; it does not make those proprietary dependencies open source.
status_note: The root initial commit on 2022-08-05 contains a full GPL-3.0 license; the first public DOL source commit is 2022-10-21 (linked above). A 2024 commit changed the repository grant to AGPL-3.0. The Developers Italia record has an anomalous legacy 'last release' date alongside its stated 2022 version, so neither was used as the source-year proxy. Current operation is supported by the official 2026 applicant portal and official user manuals. No catalog entry was added.

decision_reason: The exact public repository contains DHIS2 Core under BSD-3-Clause, and HISP UiO/Norad provide current development, maintenance, releases, installation guidance, and product-specific funding. However, the GitHub tree is a 2016 import from revision 23767, while first-party DHIS2 sources date the first DHIS2 implementation to 2006; neither the GitHub import date nor the deployment date by itself establishes when licensed source was first publicly available. Hold pending a dated pre-import licensed-source artifact or authoritative release record.

government_provenance.note: The HISP Centre at the University of Oslo leads development and maintenance, and Norad's 2024 five-year agreement commits Norwegian public funding to continue developing and maintaining the DHIS2 platform. Other public and international partners also support the specific core software; this is direct product-level funding/stewardship evidence.

public_source.note: The exact public repository contains the DHIS2 server-side Java core and REST API source, with development documentation and history accessible without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The repository root carries the full BSD 3-Clause license for DHIS2 Core source; the README and official download page confirm this exact release family is under BSD-3-Clause. Separate applications and third-party dependencies are outside this repository-level scope.

primary_evidence.note: Official DHIS2 downloads provide current stable, nightly, and development core releases with installation guidance; official documentation and the current product page describe national government deployments. This supports current distribution and product notability for the exact core platform.

product_identity: DHIS2 Core, the Java server-side component and Web API for the DHIS2 health information management platform; not the separately maintained Android capture app or web applications
agency: HISP Centre at the University of Oslo (product steward); Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (Norad) and other public/international partners support core development and maintenance
geography: Norway-hosted development and funding; global HISP network and national health systems
license: BSD-3-Clause for DHIS2 Core source in this repository; separately licensed applications and dependencies are not included
family_note: This decision concerns only the server-side core repository. DHIS2 Android Capture, web apps, metadata packages, and related tools are separate repositories and are not covered by the core root grant.
status_note: The oldest GitHub commit is dated 2016-08-30 and identifies itself as an import from upstream revision 23767; it contains code and a BSD license. DHIS2's first-party history says the first DHIS2 implementation launched in 2006, but that deployment date does not prove when licensed source first became public, and the imported SVN revision number does not date that earlier availability. Year remains null pending a dated public licensed source artifact predating or contextualizing the import. Current releases and government use are directly documented. No catalog entry was added.

decision_reason: This exact repository is the Norwegian Digitalisation Agency's Designsystemet suite of UI components, patterns, and developer packages, co-developed with other named public agencies. The repository is public; its current root grant is MIT, and the first source commit in 2022 included a BSD-3-Clause grant. Digdir announced the stable 1.0 launch and documents use in Altinn Studio and other Norwegian public services. No catalog entry was added.

government_provenance.note: Digdir's official launch page says Digdir developed this shared public-service design system together with the Norwegian Directorate for Education and Training, Norwegian Food Safety Authority, and Brønnøysund Register Centre. This is direct government authorship and stewardship evidence for the product represented by the Digdir repository.

public_source.note: The official Digdir repository is public and exposes the monorepo source for the CLI, CSS, framework-agnostic web components, React components, types, tests, and package/build configuration without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The current root LICENSE contains the full MIT grant for first-party source in this monorepo. The initial 2022 source commit used BSD-3-Clause; both exact grants are OSI-approved. External packages/dependencies retain their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: Digdir's official 2025 announcement documents the stable 1.0 release and identifies production use in Altinn Studio, toll.no, virksomhetsopplysninger, ledsagerbevis.no, and data.norge.no. The repository links public setup documentation and installable packages.

product_identity: Designsystemet, Digdir's shared Norwegian public-sector design system and component suite: CLI, CSS, React and framework-agnostic web packages, types, and design guidance
agency: Norwegian Digitalisation Agency (Digdir), with Norwegian Directorate for Education and Training, Norwegian Food Safety Authority, and Brønnøysund Register Centre
license: MIT for current first-party monorepo source; initial 2022 code was released under BSD-3-Clause, and third-party dependencies retain their own terms
family_note: This repository contains multiple first-party packages that together implement Designsystemet; the current root MIT grant was checked at repository scope. It does not cover dependencies distributed by other projects or external design assets under separate notices.
